question: Why the diplomacy screen shows a picture under its decisions, where a settings window goes, and what a ship level says of itself

addresses.name: CDiplomacyView_UpdateCustomGamePanel
addresses.comment: The last step of CDiplomacyView::Update; the view is passed on the stack. **`cgm_diplo_bg`, the picture country_diplomacy.gui lays under the decision list, belongs to a custom game**: looked up by name, and where the first byte of GetCustomGameSettings is 0 (a normal game) it is hidden (slot 14) if shown and the routine ends. In a custom game the widgets at +0x51C and +0x520..+0x524 get their slot 5, a pending rebuild flagged by the global byte 0x1A8562C is run, and the picture is shown (slot 13) if hidden. So in a normal game the picture is never on screen. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 0x78EC90 whole. The only reference to the string cgm_diplo_bg (rva 0x11DABAC) is at 0x78ECBB here. The branch on the first byte of GetCustomGameSettings ends in the element's slot 14 (+0x38) on the normal path and slot 13 (+0x34) on the custom path, both gated on its shown byte; slots 13 and 14 are Show and Hide in FINDINGS-gui.md. `mov ebx,[ebp+8]` at 0x78ECAC is the view on the stack. Wrong if the first byte is not the custom-game flag, which the record of GetCustomGameSettings and CDiplomacyView::Update's use of the same byte both say it is.

addresses.name: CPossibleModelEntry::CPossibleModelEntry
addresses.no_signature: eight stack arguments and a returned `this`; not typed
addresses.comment: The constructor of one level in `shipbuild_model_selection`'s list: a `shipbuild_possible_model_entry` window with `name` from 0x5010E0 (the country, the technology, the level), `effect` from CTechStatistics::BuildEffectsText, `change` attached to the entry's own click, and `current_model` hidden unless this is the level chosen now. Its click (slot 34, 0x807710) calls CShipBuilder::ChooseModel. **The `effect` text is BuildEffectsText with the ship's own CSubUnitDefinition as its filter** (CShipBuilder::OpenModelSelection passes the definition at the selected build type's +0x58), and with the row's level as the count of levels: only that unit type's figures, each on its own line, level 0 writing the short name and nothing after it. A government in exile asking for a level above its own takes the name from its faction's first member.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 0x807320 and its caller 0x80A260: the ctor calls BuildEffectsText(technology, out, param_6, param_7, tag), and 0x80A260 passes `*(int*)(*(int*)(this+0x198)+0x58)` as param_7 and the level as param_6. FINDINGS-techtext.md said nothing passes a filter; this is that sentence corrected.
addresses.revises: Adds what the effect text is given, the filter and the level, and the exile's name: the old comment named the function and not its arguments.

addresses.name: MessageDialog_OpenSettingWindow
addresses.comment: **A right click on a message popup**: a CMessageSettingWindow for the popup's type (+0x8C), placed by the mouse and kept on screen, added to the dialogs. Shared by all twelve CMessageDialog<T> - each constructor stores it as the right-click handler of its third observer, which the text builders attach to the background, AgreeButton, DeclineButton and CenterOK. Where it goes: x the mouse's, y the mouse's less 150; then moved back by what it passes the screen's right and bottom by, no test for the left or the top.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 0xA0D340: y = mouse[1] - 0x96; x = mouse[0]; each moved back by screen less (place + size) where that is negative, against the session's screen height +0x6B9C0 and width +0x6B9BC. Wrong if those two are not the screen, which the same two offsets are in the log row's routine 0x64BC50.
addresses.revises: Adds the placement arithmetic; 'by the mouse' said only where in general.
